hot.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights
hot.summary: The authors show that GPT-6 Astra, a general-purpose frontier LLM, can read and write neural network weights directly, without gradient descent or trained helper models. Across eight experiments it identifies what small networks were trained on from their weights, fixes and writes game-playing policies, and edits 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights to stop reasoning loops. They call this Weight-Space Programming.

hot.title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
hot.summary: The authors test whether positive views can align separately trained text and image representations. A JEPA trained on different descriptions of the same scene learns stronger alignment than one trained on corruptions of a single description. On WIT-1024, the 109M-parameter model scores .184 against DINOv2 ViT-B, exceeding Qwen2.5-72B’s .154; the theorem’s idealized assumptions limit generalization.

hot.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
hot.summary: ID-WM separates choosing intermediate states from choosing actions to make long-horizon planning in world models manageable. A diffusion model proposes nearby subgoals, and an action-conditioned model searches for actions to reach them, with planning repeated locally. In state-based PushT random-goal trials, it succeeds in 77% versus 21% for single-level world-model MPC; this result is limited to the tested benchmark setting.

hot.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
hot.summary: uni-robot-agent provides a shared tool-and-feedback harness for general-purpose models to operate robots across environments. Adapters translate common requests into environment-specific actions, while its scheduler overlaps independent reasoning and execution but orders calls that share a robot resource. On RoboDojo, zero-shot open-weight Qwen3.8-Flash-Next scores 31.39, above the published GPT-6 Astra–RoboProbe score of 28.97; this is not a matched comparison.

hot.title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
hot.summary: CoworkOS addresses complex work by letting a Main Agent direct delegated tasks while a Coordinator tracks assignments and feedback, and Subagents execute bounded work. Persistent jobs, memory, and shared resources support continuity across interruptions. In a five-round post-training case study, the mean across eight benchmark scores rose from 33.19 to 42.95; this measured increase does not isolate CoworkOS’s causal effect.

hot.title: Hinted Scaling Laws
hot.summary: The authors develop benchmark hinting to forecast downstream accuracy when smaller models score near zero. They add graded solution help, fit its relationship with model scale, and predict the unhinted score. On Delphi, logit mixing predicted 25.9% GSM8K accuracy for a 10^23-FLOP model within 3 percentage points, using models trained with at most 10^20 FLOPs. This result uses a solution-prompted teacher.

hot.title: Mistral Large 4
hot.summary: Mistral Large 4 adapts its attention architecture for long-context agents while retaining serving efficiency. It expands full-context access across more layers, then uses a learned indexer to select tokens for sparse attention. Models with similar language-modeling loss differed on SWE-bench Verified, but not knowledge evaluations; the comparisons do not show that attention alone caused every difference.

hot.title: Inverse optimization for divisor methods of apportionment
hot.summary: The authors develop an inverse method measuring regional priority adjustments needed for an observed allocation to fit a chosen divisor rule. It finds a unique mean-one weight vector by solving for one parameter. In Japan, Adams requires less adjustment than Jefferson across seven elections; its 2024 score is zero because that allocation used Adams. The score is method-relative, not a general measure of fairness.

hot.title: Subpolynomial-Query Proximal Sampling Beyond Log-Concavity
hot.summary: The authors develop a gradient-query method for sampling smooth, possibly nonconvex densities under log-Sobolev or Poincaré inequalities. It advances a chain using noisy observations, then decodes the final observation to recover a sample from the target. Under log-Sobolev conditions, its query count is subpolynomial in dimension for fixed parameters; under Poincaré conditions, this requires fixed initialization cost and divergence.

hot.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
hot.summary: Pixel co-designs a mobile-manipulation robot, demonstration interfaces, controller, and learning system so human and robot demonstrations can use shared task-space actions. A ground-anchored frame expresses head and hand targets together, which a whole-body controller translates into motion. Policies trained on human demonstrations averaged 82.0% task progress, versus 67.3% and 25.7% for alternatives; robot-data joint-space actions scored higher.

hot.title: NorthCUA Technical Report: Turbocharging Computer-Use Agents through Experience at Scale
hot.summary: NorthCUA connects task execution, outcome checking, and policy training in a shared computer-use loop. Its Harness records desktop and web interactions, while its Flywheel selects checked experience for supervised and reinforcement learning. On WebArena-Verified, Pro success rose from 69.6% to 73.9% across the same 812 tasks; this measures the full training transition, not isolated components.

hot.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
hot.summary: The authors cast pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning, and suitable reinforcement-learning updates as maximum-likelihood training with a changing data mixture. In reasoning experiments, unified schedules reach higher accuracy and coverage at larger tested compute budgets, though staged training can lead at intermediate budgets. After coding updates, a 0.76B model with 5% midtraining-data mixing scores 58.47% pass@16 versus 52.12%, limited to this continuation setup.

hot.title: Hierarchical Residuals: A Minimalist Decoupling of Residual Width from Compute Width
hot.summary: HiRes separates carried residual width from layer-computation width in Transformers. It carries a wider state between groups of ordinary PreNorm layers, which still compute at width d, using block-boundary projections and RMSNorm. In five model-size comparisons, its fitted training FLOPs to validation loss 3.00 are lower; the vanilla baseline requires 1.30× as much, but this is not a wall-clock speedup.

hot.title: Avatar Intelligence: Amplifying Human Agency Through Persistent Personal Agents
hot.summary: The authors propose Avatar Intelligence, a persistent-agent paradigm for delegating decisions while preserving user control. The system would carry a user model across tasks, act within delegated authority, and seek clarification when needed. They propose AOI, combining net user value with an oversight penalty. The paper offers a roadmap, not an implementation or evidence that oversight is reduced.

hot.title: CUA-Master: Scaling Computer-use Agents through Open-World Recursive Improvements
hot.summary: CUA-Master trains computer-use agents by turning real software tutorial workflows into executable tasks and using observed failures to guide later training. It composes reusable operations and retries failed tasks while preserving successful prefixes. Its 27-billion-parameter model improves over similarly sized UI-Mate-27B across four benchmarks and is competitive with larger systems, but the paper does not isolate which components drive gains.

hot.title: Reimagining computational quantum research with AI scientists
hot.summary: OmniQ evaluates whether AI agents can reconstruct computational quantum workflows from papers and target results, run them, and check methods and outcomes. In an audit of 60 studies, it identified 18 issues, including one unresolved case excluded from evaluation. Its Residual Agents system raised reproduction success from 68% to about 85% on 59 tasks, at $5.60 inference cost per task.

hot.title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
hot.summary: Latent Sparse Attention (LSA) speeds up key selection for long-context attention by grouping similar keys, scoring compact summaries of those groups, and retrieving selected keys for ordinary attention. In one GLM-5.3-FLASH attention layer at 10M tokens, Distilled-LSA Flat prefills 22.7× faster and decodes 4.6× faster than baseline sparse attention, while staying within four accuracy points on RULER; these results are not end-to-end speedups or proof of equivalent performance on all tasks.

hot.title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
hot.summary: The authors evaluate ten frozen visual representations for whether small probes can read visible scene structure, retain objects after they leave view, predict spatial updates under camera motion, and select goal-directed actions. VideoMAE’s out-of-view bearing error is 36.45°, versus DINOv2’s 65.38°, despite DINOv2’s stronger visible-scene readouts. These offline tests do not establish online memory or reliable robot behavior.

hot.title: Statistical Foundations of Reinforcement Learning: A Non-Asymptotic Perspective
hot.summary: The monograph synthesizes finite-sample guarantees for tabular reinforcement learning across generative-model, online, and offline data settings, comparing algorithmic upper bounds with minimax lower bounds. It explains how sampling conditions shape effective methods and uncertainty strategies. Online, MVP achieves high-probability regret O(min{√(SAH³K), HK}) for every K ≥ 1, matching the minimax lower bound up to logarithmic factors in finite-horizon nonstationary MDPs.

hot.title: SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding
hot.summary: SpecOPD trains speculative-decoding drafters with branch-parallel on-policy supervision. It samples continuations at separate positions in reference text, scores them with the target model, and reuses computation for shared prefixes. On Qwen3-8B with DFlash, mean acceptance length rises from 2.649 to 3.747 tokens per verification round, a 41.45% increase; gains vary across settings.

likes.title: FlatCake: A Flat KVCache Storage Architecture for LLM Serving
likes.summary: FlatCake places language-model KV caches across DRAM and SSD for reuse of long histories. It assigns immutable blocks at creation, groups session data in layer-major order, and restores SSD data through coalesced reads to GPU memory. On a Claude Code replay with DeepSeek-V4-Flash at 1.0 QPS, it records 7.57-second mean TTFT and 98.3K tokens/s, versus Mooncake’s 12.24 seconds and 61.6K tokens/s.

likes.title: Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake
likes.summary: The simulation-trained model improves psychiatric intake conversations by practicing multi-turn encounters with simulated patients and receiving rewards for clinical reasoning, communication, and safety. In a randomized, double-blind crossover study, it received higher psychiatrist transcript ratings than its identically prompted base model in 46 of 60 matched scenario pairs (76.7%). This supports improvement in controlled text encounters, not real-patient safety or effectiveness.

likes.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
likes.summary: ThinkWorld addresses robot-learning by grounding robot actions and annotated human hand motion in a shared discrete Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD) vocabulary. It trains on action-unlabeled videos by rewarding tokens whose predicted futures match observed futures. At deployment, a separate expert predicts continuous actions. In real-robot trials, it achieved 94.4% macro success across six task-condition combinations and succeeded in 52/60 OOD trials.

likes.title: How to Loop Your Transformer: Loop Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference
likes.summary: The authors study looping, which reuses transformer weights for repeated computation, in dense decoder-only models. They compare loop designs and shifted parallel looping. In tested over-trained conditions, two-loop models at 80 tokens per parameter reach a given DCLM validation bits-per-byte with fewer training FLOPs than vanilla models at 160 tokens per parameter, without establishing general efficiency or latency gains.

likes.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations
likes.summary: EmbeddingGemma 2 maps text, images, audio, and video into an embedding space for retrieval. Modality encoders turn media into tokens that a transformer pools into a vector; modular configurations omit encoders not needed. On MSEB(Retrieval), native audio scores 69.54 MRR@10 versus 57.59 for ASR/text, but uses more parameters. An intermediate MMEB-v2 ablation improves image and video scores, while visual-document performance remains nearly unchanged.

likes.title: Timestral
likes.summary: Timestral is a time-series forecasting model that learns across series and forecasts new ones without retraining. It keeps observed history available while adding separate prediction positions, and assigns covariates roles so known-future inputs can be used without exposing future targets. Timestral-209M ranks first among compared models on six metrics across three benchmarks; this does not isolate DHF’s contribution.

likes.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
likes.summary: GEPA-Curator improves prompt optimization by selecting task experiences for learning and retrieving a prior success when a task fails. It maintains task histories, skips tasks unlikely to provide useful signal, and gives the optimizer a same-task reference when available. In experiments, it scores 88.6% on GitLab validation; gains vary by setting and do not establish that every failure is noisy.

likes.title: NyoomFloat12: Accelerating LLM Inference via Lossless 12-Bit Weight Compression
likes.summary: The authors introduce NF12, a lossless format that stores BF16 weights in 12 bits and reconstructs them in a GPU-friendly, fixed-length pattern. It exploits concentrated exponent values and handles rare exceptions separately. On a shared-prefix Qwen3-32B rollout workload, NF12 reaches a peak of 787 output tokens per second versus BF16’s 310, a schedule-dependent 2.54× ratio; gains are not universal.

likes.title: Learning Quality-Controllable Robot Policies with Iterative Hindsight Relabeling
likes.summary: QCP lets users request execution quality by labeling successful trajectories with rule-based scores and conditioning a policy on those labels. It collects successful rollouts at the highest label, relabels data by measured quality, and retrains. On a conveyor, its highest-bin policy raises end-effector speed from 188.6 to 257.6 mm/s and throughput from 8.2 to 13.0 cans per minute versus BC.

likes.title: Multi-Token Prediction Done Right
likes.summary: Soft-MTP changes multi-token prediction training so MTP heads learn from the model’s own next-token predictions while the shared output head retains cross-entropy training. It recovers this self-distillation signal through gradient routing, without computing a vocabulary-wide KL loss. Across 167M–1.2B models, it improves validation loss and eight-task average accuracy over standard MTP; evidence is limited to tested scales.

likes.title: Know, then Draw: A New Learning Paradigm for Visual Generation
likes.summary: The authors introduce a two-stage text-to-image system: an autoregressive (AR) model predicts visual tokens from a prompt, then diffusion renders pixels from them. They freeze the pretrained AR backbone while training the renderer. A roughly 3-billion-parameter model trained with 6,600 H100 GPU-hours scores 0.86 on GenEval and 87.78 on DPG-Bench, supporting this recipe but not universal superiority or optimal compute allocation.

likes.title: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory
likes.summary: L3G-World generates interactive video worlds using a revisable 3D Gaussian scene memory that stores video-VAE features. It renders this memory into latent conditioning for each video chunk, then updates it by adding missing content and refining visible Gaussians. On DL3DV loop-closure tests, it achieves 16.00 self-consistency PSNR versus 13.96 for Spatia; Matrix-Game 3.0 has lower LPIPS, and tests use static scenes.

likes.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
likes.summary: SynthAPI lets researchers test how tool, task, and database-state diversity affect training for agents that use stateful tools. It varies apps, tasks per app, starting database profiles, and distractor data across training budgets. On held-out high-compute runs, its composition-aware scaling law reaches a 0.0285 MAE, versus 0.1706 for task count alone, with extrapolation up to 16×; validation covers one synthesis pipeline.
